title: folio-insights — Book-Extraction UAT
subtitle: First UAT · one-chapter pipeline de-risk (Trial Advocacy Ch01) · findings, not yet rubric-scored
rubric_version: extraction-quality-v1 — DRAFT (awaiting Damien's lock; no scoring until locked, policy 3)

spend.notes: one-chapter de-risk run; ~$10/book → ~$30 est. for all 3 books. Cost is not the constraint; correctness is.

sections.title: Pipeline works end-to-end on real book text
sections.body_md: The **live v1 pipeline runs end-to-end** on a real chapter and produces good output: **621 knowledge units** (mean confidence 0.87 — 573 high / 44 med / 4 low), **529 distinct valid FOLIO IRIs**, and a SHACL-conformant OWL export. unit_type mix: advice 313 · principle 258 · pitfall 35 · procedural_rule 14 · citation 1. So the core works — the items below are what gate an at-scale run.

sections.title: All deterministic oracles PASS
sections.body_md:
The gestalt's deterministic layer (which can run **before** the rubric locks):

- **folio-python IRI existence + branch consistency** (15-of-529 sample): **15/15 pass**, 0 mismatches (18,326 concepts loaded).
- **SHACL `export --validate`**: **conforms = TRUE** — Shapes / IRI-Uniqueness / Referential-Integrity / Namespace-Consistency all PASS (67 task classes, 440 triples).
- **`verify-iris`**: N/A — needs the v2 DID/shard registry, which v1 extract/discover/export don't populate.

sections.title: B1 — Bridge venv deps undeclared (FIXED this session)
sections.body_md: `python-docx`, `rapidfuzz`, `marisa-trie` are imported via the folio-enrich sys.path bridge but were **never declared in folio-insights' manifest**. Their silent absence killed `.docx` ingestion **and** ALL FOLIO IRI matching (every tag degraded to an un-IRI'd proposed_class). **Fixed:** declared as core deps → 529 valid IRIs, 0 spurious proposed classes. Compounded in `docs/solutions/`.

sections.title: B2 — .docx ingestion broken (BLOCKER · [CE])
sections.body_md: folio-enrich's `WordIngestor` reads only `document.paragraphs`; this book's prose lives in `<w:sdt>` content-controls → **0 chars read** → the pipeline falls back to reading the raw `.docx` ZIP archive as UTF-8 → 'units' of PK-header binary. **Every Trial Advocacy chapter is `.docx`.** Worked around via `<w:t>` XML extraction for the de-risk run. Fix = traverse sdt/tables/textboxes in the ingestor **or** add a folio-insights docx→text preprocessor. Touches pipeline structure + sibling repo → `/ce:plan` next session.

sections.title: B3 — OpenAI provider unusable → run on Google (decision)
sections.body_md: folio-enrich's `OpenAICompatProvider` forces `response_format: json_object`, but the extraction prompts never contain the literal word 'json' → **400 on every call** (+ TPM 429s). **Decision: run the campaign on Google** — `GOOGLE_API_KEY` is present + valid and the default `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` works and is cheap. No folio-insights change needed; the upstream prompt fix is folio-enrich's scope.

sections.title: B4 — Discovery→Export chain broken (BLOCKER · [CE])
sections.body_md: Discovery's LLM stages call a non-existent `provider.generate()` (providers expose `complete`/`chat`) → they **silently fail** → discovered tasks get **no FOLIO IRIs**; CLI `discover` never writes `review.db`; the OWL serializer then crashes on null `folio_iri`. (The SHACL PASS above required manually seeding review.db + minting task IRIs.) The `.generate()`→`complete/chat` rename may be a one-liner, but the review.db-write + null-IRI handling are structural → `/ce:plan`.

sections.title: Q1 — Provenance spans do NOT trace to source (challenges the thesis) ⭐
sections.body_md: **The most important finding for the rubric.** Units are **LLM-distilled paraphrases**, and their `original_span{start,end}` offsets do **not** point at the source text they summarize. So today the pipeline is closer to *abstractive summarization with a broken back-pointer* than to true extraction. This bears directly on how strict `RUB-EXTRACT-05/06/07` should be — **I've asked you this on the Proof doc.** Do you want these to fail outright (forcing a pipeline fix to true extraction) or score borderline-while-we-fix?

sections.title: Q2 — Semantically wrong FOLIO branch mappings (homonyms)
sections.body_md: IRIs are valid FOLIO nodes (deterministic check passes) but the **concept choice** is often a homonym mis-match: 'Expert testimony' → **Location**, 'Rule 26(a)(1)' → **Location**, 'Daubert/Frye' → **Asset Type**. The four-path tagger picks lexically-plausible but semantically wrong concepts. This is the strongest argument for the **FOLIO-MCP semantic gate** (gestalt rule) in judging, and a pipeline-tuning target.
